chunks: 5 - He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who reported from al-Hasan ibn Ulail al-Anzi, who reported from Abdul Karim ibn Muhammad, who reported from Ali ibn Salemah, from Abu Aslam Muhammad ibn Fakhar, from Abu Hayyaj Abdullah ibn Amir, who said:

When the sad news of al-Husayn's (peace be upon him) martyrdom reached Madinah, Asma bint Aqil ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with her) came out with a group of her women and went to the grave of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), clung to it, and sobbed bitterly beside it. Then she turned to the Muhajireen and the Ansar and said:

"What will you say when the Prophet says to you on the Day of Judgment, and the truth will indeed be heard: 'You deserted my family, or were you absent, while the truth will be gathered before the master of the affair. You handed them over into the hands of the oppressors, so none among you today has an intercessor before God. There was no one at the morning of al-Taff (Kerbala) when death came to them, and none to repel it from them.'"
He said: "We never saw as many wailing men and women on any other day."

key_terms.الطف: Al-Taff - The plain of Kerbala where Imam Husayn was martyred in 61 AH
key_terms.المهاجرين والأنصار: The Muhajireen and Ansar - the two main groups of early Muslims in Madinah
key_terms.عترتي: Itrati - My family/progeny, referring to the Prophet's descendants (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What did Asma bint Aqil say at the Prophet's grave after Husayn's martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration describes the grief that overtook Madinah when news of Imam Husayn's martyrdom at Kerbala arrived. Asma bint Aqil ibn Abi Talib, a member of the Prophet's extended family, went to the Prophet's grave and delivered a powerful poetic reproach to the Muhajireen and Ansar for failing to protect the Prophet's family. Her elegy invoked the Day of Judgment to shame those who stood by while the Prophet's grandson was killed.
